title: A gold sunset with a glowing sun, round 10's sunbeams back, and leaner meteors
intro: This round answers your round 11 notes, copying from the packs as in round 11, each option against round 11 with its cost. High frames cost 3.65 ms at most (round 11: 3.30, budget 3.0), Low at 1080p 0.89 ms (budget 0.9) and Potato at 720p 0.31 ms (budget 0.4), per frame against the same view with shaders off; the sea sunset is over its High budget, as in rounds 10 and 11, because round 10's rays you picked cost 0.30 ms there.

scenes.name: Sunset: gold instead of pink, and a sun that glows
scenes.question: You said to listen to the critic: round 11's sunset was pink-lilac where your photo is amber-gold, and the sun was a thin white sliver with no glow. Causes, measured: the pink is Photon's own dusk tint (it lowers green below blue in the sunlight and in the whole sky); the missing glow is because our glare only drew round the part of the disk in clear sky, so a sun just under a cloud got none, and it held a ten-thousandth of the sun's light where Photon's bloom spreads about 12 %. Now Photon's own per-hour sun tint setting is set to gold for the sunlight and the glow round the sun, while the upper sky keeps a near-neutral tint so it stays blue, and the sun gets a wide warm glow like BSL's and Photon's, drawn over the clouds in front of it when they are thin and sunlit (the photo's sun bursting through). Cost: gold +0.00 to +0.04 ms, glow +0.00 to +0.09 ms on High. A new, B round 11.
scenes.notePrompt: Gold enough? Is the glow the right size and strength?

options.label: Gold, with glow (default)
options.critic: Critic 7: Answers the note on colour. The sky, clouds and haze are amber-gold from the horizon up (horizon 182,146,92 against round 11's 186,136,106), and the upper sky is no longer lilac. Round 10's fan of rays is back over the sun, and the islands read through gold air. Two gaps to the photo and BSL remain. The sea stays navy (25,44,69, darker than round 11's 42,46,74), so the lower half does not take the sunset. The sun is still a white sliver under the cloud; in the 2x crop its glow is only a faint round lobe above the sliver, about 3 luma above no glow. Fix: make the sea reflect the gold sky, and judge the glow on a view where the sun is clear of cloud.

scenes.name: Round 10's sunbeams on Photon's sky, without the near haze
scenes.question: You picked round 10's rays (C) and said Photon's looked like artifacting (A) and rays off was very hazy (B). Round 10's rays are back as the default on High and Ultra, now over Photon's sky. The haze: Photon's dusk haze lay right up to your feet, so the near grass came out lifted and grey (round 11 69,67,41 against round 10's 38,45,15, bottom of the frame). Its haze now starts 32 blocks out and grows from there, so distance still fades into gold air but the ground round you keeps its colour (now 40,56,19). Cost on High: round 10's rays +0.01 to +0.30 ms (Photon's were +0.00 to +0.02), the clear near air +0.00 ms. Round 10's rays are the dearest part of this round: they read 16 points of the sky on the line to the sun for every sky pixel near a low sun; Photon's cost almost nothing because they read a small shadow map. A cheaper round-10 look (fewer reads, or Photon's march with round 10's lanes) is next round's work if you keep these. A new, B round 11, C round 10 (what you picked).
scenes.notePrompt: Do the rays read the way you liked in round 10? Is the near field clear enough?

options.label: Round 10's rays, clear near air (default)
options.critic: Critic 8: Answers both notes. The near grass has its colour back: the bottom of the frame is 38,56,20, against round 11's 67,67,40 and round 10's 37,45,16. The light lanes falling from the hill are round 10's, drawn on the ground as in C, and the gold air stays in the distance. The horizon is gold where C's is pink. Two flaws remain. The far-left hills sink into a flat beige wall of haze. The fan above the sun that B drew is gone, because round 10's rays draw lanes on the ground, not in the sky. Next: a cheaper version of these rays. They cost up to +0.30 ms and make the sea sunset the round's worst frame, at 3.65 ms.

scenes.name: Leaner meteors, like your photos
scenes.question: You said the storm meteors looked bulky next to your photos. Each streak is now a hairline about half as wide, a third longer, fainter, and it fades in and out along its length with no bright head, as in the photos. Round 11's clip was also a 1:1 crop of the screen, which doubled every streak's width on your phone; both clips now show a wider part of the sky at the size the game draws it. Meteors also wait until the sun is well down (the critic's contrail at dusk). Cost on the wide night view: A 2.94 ms, B 2.94 ms (budget 3.0): the lean shape costs nothing extra. A lean (default), B round 11's shape, same view.

options.label: Lean storm (default), clip
options.critic: Critic 7: Answers the note. Each streak is now a hairline, about half round 11's width, and peaks at 122 luma over the sky where round 11's peaked at 188. That is much closer to the Perseid photo. It still differs from the photos in one way: every streak runs parallel at the same angle and about the same length, so the storm reads as rain or scratches. In the photos the streaks radiate from one point and range from short to long. Also, a streak that crosses a thin cloud breaks into dashes. Fix: radiate the streaks from a radiant point and vary their length and brightness.

options.label: Round 11's storm shape, clip
options.critic: Critic 5: Round 11's shape on the same crop: thicker, soft-edged streaks up to 188 luma. Beside A they look bulky, as the owner said.

scenes.name: Diamond: glassier and more reflective
scenes.question: Why r011's copy was not glassier, measured: Stay True's art is the same brightness as Faithful's; its glint is animated (one 10 s still frame, then 7 glint frames of 1/20 s), so a still shows it 3% of the time; it lost r010's domed normal map (24 deg tilt -> 2 deg, flat); and our shader gave a polished non-metal only a sky reflection clamped at the horizon, so every pixel of a flat face mirrored the same bright horizon: +15% brighter, -24% colour, -39% contrast on the diamond face. So this round shows three ways forward on a diamond floor and pillar, looking into a low sun, where a polished surface shows its reflection. These two views are on round 12's shader (the sun no longer shows through the cloud as a hard oval); its gold sky lifts the gem floors 3 to 6 luma over the numbers below, which were measured on round 11's shader next to the r010 and r011 gems.
scenes.notePrompt: Which reads most like polished gem? Too mirror-like anywhere?

options.label: A: Faithful gems, polished
options.desc: Your r010 diamond and emerald (Faithful 64x art; the emerald in the diamond's direction), both on the diamond's domed normal map and polished (smoothness 240, diamond's reflectance on both). Texture-only. Into the sun every block catches its own sun glint; r011's flat streak of bright horizon is gone (floor brightness 116 vs r011 118, r010 129).
options.critic: Critic 5: Re-shot on round 12's shader after the fix: the hard oval through the cloud is gone (it was the sun disk passing 1-2 % through the cloud, not the glow); the sun behind the cloud base is now a smooth glow with the crisp sliver below it. Texture unchanged from g12a: clean polished Faithful diamond, but every block has the same white hotspot in the same place, so the floor reads as a grid of lamps.

options.label: B: Stay True's glass, no squares
options.desc: Stay True's diamond as it is, glint and all; its emerald replaced by the same glass face in Stay True's emerald colours, so the nested squares are gone. Same polish and domed normal as A. Same glint per block as A on Stay True's art (floor 116).
options.critic: Critic 5: Re-shot on round 12's shader after the fix: the hard oval through the cloud is gone (it was the sun disk passing 1-2 % through the cloud, not the glow); the sun behind the cloud base is now a smooth glow with the crisp sliver below it. Stay True's glass face: in a still it is almost the same as A, corner bevels and one dot per block, no glassier.

options.label: C: real reflections (shader)
options.desc: A's textures, plus a shader change: polished gems reflect what is really around them (the sky and clouds, the ground, the pillar) the way our metals already do, instead of one horizon colour. Works with B's art too. Shader cost on High at 1440p, QF_GEM_SSR on vs off on the same view: +0.18 ms on the first glint view (2.43 -> 2.61 ms against shaders off), +0.17 on the second, +0.05 on the lit view; it scales with how much of the screen is gem, and costs nothing with no gems in view or below Medium. The most glass-like here: the floor mirrors the clouds and pillars, darker (106) with the same contrast. Each block reads a little cushioned, from the domed normal map.
options.critic: Critic 7: Re-shot on round 12's shader after the fix: the hard oval through the cloud is gone (it was the sun disk passing 1-2 % through the cloud, not the glow); the sun behind the cloud base is now a smooth glow with the crisp sliver below it. Still the only option that reads as polished gem: sky and sun reflected, changing block to block. The reflection still wobbles (wet plastic more than cut stone).

scenes.name: HUD: three Quest Forge directions
scenes.question: Our own art, Faithless's hearts and food kept. Iron: the main menu's forged plates, lavender rim, ember selection, molten XP. Arcane: indigo and gold, gem corners, emerald XP, runes in the boss channel. Banner: walnut and brass, red banner selection, gold XP, red ribbon boss bar. 1.7.10 draws every boss bar from one 182 x 5 strip; a taller framed bar (one per boss) needs a small qf-tweaks hook. The designs cannot be drawn in game yet, because QuestForge.zip's widgets.png sits on top of the pack's HUD, so there are no in-game frames this round (the three we shot had chat covering the hearts and the food bar draining). Instead, M is an offline mock of round 11 and all three directions, our art at 1.7.10's layout, with each direction's hotbar and selection; shipping one means replacing QuestForge.zip's hotbar too.
